I ran alchemy on this as a design pass and stopped before writing any code. One decision is yours first: adding a linter, which would be the project's first dependency.

## What I found

**Decision:** split billing out of `src/orders/index.js` into `src/billing/index.js` as a module beside orders and shipping (the record calls this **SPLIT**).

- **Design:** billing becomes one function, `invoiceFor(customer, lines)`. It holds `TAX_BP`, `DISCOUNT_TIERS`, the check that rejects a country with no tax rate, and the invoice shape. It imports nothing. `placeOrder` keeps the empty-order check, calls `invoiceFor`, and saves.
- **Deciding fact:** all 24 finance billing commits (`FIN` tickets) in 26 weeks edited the file that also stores the order and sets its status. Three of them broke order lifecycle behaviour and needed a fix the next day (ORD-82, ORD-85, ORD-88). No single commit was both billing and order lifecycle work, so the two change for separate reasons.
- **Assumption I made:** the "no tax rate for country" check is a billing rule, because it came in as FIN-214. If the product owner considers it order validation, it stays in `placeOrder`, and billing would have to export the rate table for it.

## Why it matters

- **If you do it:** a weekly rate or discount-tier change edits only `src/billing/index.js`. Billing has no import of the repository, so a rule change can't leave an order stored without its status or lines.
  - What you get is less risk on each change, not a simpler structure. The import graph gains one file and one import and gets no simpler. The split is justified because the requirement's first done-when condition can't be met without a separate file.
- **If you don't:** every weekly rule change edits the file that stores orders, sets their status, and handles cancelling and reading them. So far that has caused a lifecycle regression about once every eight rule changes.

## Do this first

1. **Decide how to enforce the new boundary.** The rule "billing imports nothing" has to ship in the same PR as the module (CLAUDE.md §6). The repo has no linter and no dependencies, and adding the first devDependency is your call.
   - **I recommend** `eslint` + `eslint-plugin-boundaries` with an `eslint.architecture.mjs` file. This is the skill library's JavaScript pattern, and it catches a bad import in the editor.
   - **The fallback** is a `node:test` check that parses the imports in `src/billing/`. It needs no dependency, but it only catches a bad import when the tests run.

   Once you choose, I implement it as one PR: the rule config first, then `src/billing/index.js`, the change to `placeOrder`, and a `src/billing/` line in `README.md`. The test files stay untouched.
2. After merge, re-check the outcome on 2027-01-11 or at the 8th billing commit after merge, whichever comes first. Use `git log --name-only -- src/` and confirm no billing commit touched `src/orders/`.

## What I did not check

- **`npm test` has not been run.** Nothing is implemented yet. After the change, run `npm test` and confirm all 13 tests pass with no test file changed.
- **Whether the change history still matches the code.** This folder isn't a git repo, so I couldn't confirm `main` is still at `9c41e07`. The code does match the latest commits listed (FIN-224, FIN-214, ORD-90). Close it with `git rev-parse main` in the real repo.
- **Whether CI runs `npm test` and blocks merges.** There's no pipeline config here, so check the shop-api CI settings.
- **Whether the current tests existed when the three regressions shipped.** Today's suite would catch all three. Check with `git log --follow test/orders.test.js`.
